top_choice_rationale: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a molecular-design achievement with a clear physical-chemical core: pKa-tuned lipids that are near neutral in blood and cationic in the endosome, plus controlled self-assembly and lipid phase behaviour, solve packaging and cytosolic release of a large polyanion. It is the most mature candidate (approved medicines since 2018, global use), transfers across siRNA, mRNA and gene-editing cargo, and, if the citation is written on the carrier, is distinct from the 2023 Medicine payload prize. Cullis, Hope and Anderson cover the Vancouver and Boston lineages, though the third seat (Anderson versus Madden) remains contestable. Targeted protein degradation ranks second as the strongest purely chemical idea but is less mature and has a two-strand attribution problem.
recusal_note: Field proximity: my research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is adjacent to the ionizable lipid nanoparticle proposal (P002); no personal, collaborative or institutional tie to any nominee apparent from profile.
